headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: xonsh can read/write files and egress broadly, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no shared channel, so other risks are mostly low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-nlp and xonsh. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while xonsh uses shell/stdin/stdout and filesystem, but there is no default bridge for xonsh to ingest awesome-nlp outputs as instructions.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from awesome-nlp into xonsh as shell input, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not copy outputs into shell prompts.
Store any shared artifacts in read-only form.
Use explicit quoting when pasting text into xonsh.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared workspace is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no I/O, while xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is possible only if operators place sensitive files where xonsh can read them; blast radius is limited by the docs-only, non-runnable nature of awesome-nlp.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a filesystem location readable by xonsh, leakage becomes plausible.
IF xonsh is pointed at a workspace containing secrets, those contents can flow to its outputs or network calls.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Mount a read-only workspace for xonsh.
Disable network egress for xonsh when handling sensitive files.
Review shell history before sharing logs.
requires-engineering: add per-directory access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend with xonsh over mutable resources. xonsh can write the filesystem, but there is no second writer or overlapping mutable scope documented in awesome-nlp.
conditions: IF a separate runnable agent is added with write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp as a reference-only artifact.
Avoid sharing writable directories with additional agents.
Use one writer per workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locking if another writer is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a curated list, not an action-taking agent, so xonsh is unlikely to treat its output as authoritative by default. The main pathway is manual reuse of list content inside shell workflows; because xonsh can execute commands, mistakes can cascade, but the pair lacks an automatic handoff.
conditions: IF an operator pastes list entries from awesome-nlp into xonsh commands without verification, errors can cascade.
IF xonsh scripts are built from unreviewed text sourced from awesome-nlp, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Verify any copied commands before execution.
Use a review step before running generated shell snippets.
Keep awesome-nlp content as reference only.
Log command provenance in notes.
requires-engineering: add automated validation for pasted commands.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy conflict is documented for either agent. awesome-nlp is a non-runnable open-source list, and xonsh's profile does not indicate PHI, EU PII, or special compliance obligations, so no compliance breach pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later used to process regulated data, compliance review is required.
IF a residency or retention policy is added to xonsh, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair.
Document data classes before deployment.
Check retention settings for any added logging.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
